motivation.problems: Engineers in this catalog work on services where several processes share state and any of them can stop at any moment. The tasks show five recurring problems. First, duplicate effects after retries or worker restarts, as in pdk-zulip-outgoing-webhook-delivery, pdk-elsa-external-callbacks-exactly-once and wechatpy-replay-safe-callback-consumption. Second, lost notifications when a broker or cache is down after the database commit, as in pdk-fitnet-contract-pass-offer-pipeline and kwatch-durable-insight-delivery-outbox. Third, stale writers that return after takeover, as in throttled-py-fenced-expiring-store-leases and restic-conditional-backend-writes. Fourth, limits and counters that hold in one process but not across instances, as in pdk-pulpcore-domain-storage-quota and eshop-catalog-order-stock-reservations. Fifth, partial state after a crash, as in go-diskfs-crash-recoverable-fat-metadata-62a2 and pdk-gitea-oci-chunked-upload-cluster. The cluster tasks are system design; the single-component tasks are fault tolerance. Most specs also require that existing behaviour keeps working during the change, so a fix that blocks all writes does not pass. Time bounds such as 45 seconds after recovery turn vague reliability goals into testable ones.
motivation.how_tasks_exemplify: Each task pins a real open source repository at a base commit and gives the agent a short written spec with time bounds, such as recovery within 45 seconds. Cluster tasks supply databases, caches or brokers locally or through a compose file, and the instruction says the agent runs separate processes for each role. Docker is unavailable inside the agent container, so the agent starts local services itself. The agent produces a patch to the repository. The verifier runs in a separate environment, applies the patch and hidden tests, and kills or pauses processes and services to check the stated behaviour. The tests also check that existing behaviour listed in a keep-working section still passes.
prompt_patterns: A production symptom with its mechanism, then a bulleted list of measurable requirements with time limits, as in pdk-immich-hard-storage-quota-holds.
A missing capability stated in the form 'X cannot do Y', followed by dense behavioural paragraphs, as in restic-conditional-backend-writes.
A story-style problem report from a team, then 'To close this out' requirements, as in eshop-catalog-order-stock-reservations.
A requirements list plus an explicit list of exported names and signatures to implement, as in tests-half-go-diskfs-crash-recoverable-fat-metadata-62a2.
A closing environment paragraph giving the repo path, service start commands, build command and the note that Docker is unavailable, as in pdk-grist-fenced-doc-worker-failover.
open_questions: Hidden tests and graders were not described here, so how failures are injected (kill, pause, network cut) in each task is UNKNOWN beyond what the instruction states.

The agent environment has no Docker, yet environment/docker-compose.yaml exists for grist and immich. It is unclear whether the agent container gets those services through compose or starts local copies; diagrams show them as services.

For wild-workouts, cortex, buildbot, dialogporten and aodh no compose file is in the files, so the location of PostgreSQL, Redis and RabbitMQ (local to the container or sidecar) is inferred from the instruction and Dockerfile.
Whether the 217 tasks should be split into system design (multi-instance) and fault tolerance (single component) in the catalog is not stated; the sample split here is by reading each instruction.
Batch names (system-design-cohere-ots, alpharecon-deepswe-binary) suggest different authoring pipelines; their grading format was not inspected.
